neet_che_u20_t03_1.working: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with aniline at the para position. This gives p-aminoazobenzene, which is aniline yellow.

neet_che_u20_t03_2.working: Free -NH2 activates the ring so strongly that it gives polysubstitution, and it is easily oxidised by HNO3. Acetylation moderates this activation, protects the -NH2, and favours para substitution.

neet_che_u20_t03_3.working: Propan-2-ol has a CH3CH(OH)- group. It is oxidised to acetone, which gives the iodoform test. Methanol, propan-1-ol and pentan-3-one do not.

neet_che_u20_t03_4.working: Acetanilide is white, m.p. about 114 °C (II). p-Nitroacetanilide is pale yellow, m.p. about 214 °C (IV). Aniline yellow comes from diazo coupling (III). Iodoform is yellow with an antiseptic smell, m.p. about 119 °C (I).

neet_che_u20_t03_5.working: A is true. B is false: the p-isomer crystallises from ethanol and the o-isomer stays in the filtrate. C is true. D is true: KI with NaOCl generates the hypoiodite needed. E is false: 4 mol I2 are used per mole of ethanol (1 for oxidation to acetaldehyde, 3 for iodination). So A, C and D are correct.
